questions.question: According to Article ______ of the Constitution of India, it shall be the duty of every citizen of India to develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**51A.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Article 51A:-**

 
 
• **​Article 51A deals with fundamental duties of citizens of India. **
 
• **These fundamental duties were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976, **and they provide a set of moral and civic obligations that citizens are expected to follow for the betterment of society and the nation as a whole.
 
• There are 11 fundamental duties listed in Article 51A:-
 
 
• To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag, and the National Anthem.
 
• To cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom.
 
• To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• To defend the country and render national service when called upon.
 
• To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood among all people of India transcending religious, linguistic, and regional or sectional diversities.
 
• To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.
 
• To protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures.
 
• **To develop scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform.**
 
• To safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
 
• To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity.
 
• To provide opportunities for education to their children or wards between the ages of six and fourteen years.

questions.question: According to Koeppen’s Scheme, which type of climate is denoted by ‘Cwg’ in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Monsoon with dry winter.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Köppen's scheme:-**

 
 
• **It is also known as the Köppen climate classification, is a widely used system for classifying and describing the world's climates based on temperature and precipitation patterns. **
 
• It was developed by the Russian-German climatologist Wladimir Köppen in the early 20th century and has undergone several modifications since then.
 
• The Köppen climate classification system divides the Earth's climates into five main types, each designated by a specific letter code:
 
 
• Tropical (A): These climates are characterized by high temperatures year-round and abundant precipitation. They are typically found in equatorial regions and include tropical rainforests and savannas.
 
• Dry (B): Dry climates are characterized by low precipitation levels. They are further divided into three subtypes:
 
 
• BWh: Hot desert climates, with extremely high temperatures and very low rainfall.
 
• BWk: Cold desert climates, similar to hot deserts but with colder winters.
 
• BSh/BSk: Steppe climates, with moderate temperatures and low rainfall.
 
 
 
• 
 
Temperate (C): Temperate climates have distinct seasons and moderate precipitation. They are divided into three subtypes: Cfa/Cwa, Cfb/Cwb, Csa/Csb: 

 
 
• 
 
Continental (D): Continental climates have a wide temperature range and moderate precipitation. They are divided into two subtypes: Dfa/Dwa, Dfb/Dwb.

 
 
• 
 
Polar (E): Polar climates are characterized by extremely cold temperatures and very low precipitation. They are divided into two subtypes: ET, EF.

 
 
 
 
• **Koeppen's climate classification scheme designates the "Cwg" code for a specific type of climate in India. **
 
 
• In this classification system, "C" represents a temperate or mesothermal climate, "w" indicates a dry winter season, and "g" stands for a hot summer.
 
• Therefore, the "Cwg" climate in India is a temperate climate with a dry winter and a hot summer.
 
• This type of climate is found in certain regions of northern India, particularly in areas such as parts of Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh [IMAGE: https://geography4u.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/climate-zones-in-india-map-768x1024.jpg]

questions.question: In cells, proteins are synthesised in _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ribosome.**__ 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ribosomes:-**

 
 
• They are complex molecular machines composed of RNA and protein molecules.
 
• They exist in all living cells, from bacteria to eukaryotes, and are essential for protein synthesis.
 
• **The primary function of ribosomes is to synthesize proteins through a process called translation. **
 
• They read the genetic information encoded in mRNA (messenger RNA) and use it to assemble amino acids in the correct order to form a protein chain.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mitochondria:-**

 
 
• Mitochondria are double-membraned organelles found in the cells of eukaryotic organisms.
 
• They have an outer membrane and an inner membrane that encloses the mitochondrial matrix.
 
• The inner membrane is highly folded into structures called cristae, which increase its surface area for energy production.
 
• One of the primary functions of mitochondria is to generate energy through aerobic respiration.
 
• This process involves the conversion of nutrients, particularly glucose, into adenosine triphosphate (ATP), which is the cell's primary energy currency.
 
• This process occurs in the mitochondria's inner membrane, specifically in the cristae.
 
 
 
• **Golgi apparatus:-**
 
 
• It is also known as the Golgi complex or Golgi body
 
• It is a membranous organelle found in eukaryotic cells.
 
• It consists of a series of flattened membrane-bound sacs or cisternae arranged in stacks, along with associated vesicles.
 
 
 
• **Nucleus:-**
 
 
• It is a membrane-bound organelle found in eukaryotic cells.
 
• It contains the cell's genetic material, including DNA, and serves as the control center of the cell. 
 
• The nucleus is typically spherical and surrounded by a double-layered membrane known as the nuclear envelope.

questions.question: What is Typhlops?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Blind snake**__ .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Typhlops:-**

 
 
• **It is a genus of blind snakes, also known as worm snakes, which belong to the family Typhlopidae. **
 
• These snakes are found in various regions around the world, including Africa, Asia, the Americas, and some islands in the Pacific.
 
• Blind snakes are characterized by their small size, cylindrical bodies, and reduced eyes covered by scales. They are non-venomous and mainly feed on ants and termites, using their specialized jaws and teeth to consume their prey. Due to their fossorial (burrowing) nature and secretive habits, they are not commonly encountered by humans.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Sea snake:** Sea snakes belong to a completely different family and environment. They are part of the Elapidae family and are adapted to living in marine environments. They are venomous and possess fully functional vision to navigate and hunt in the water.
 
• **Glass snakes**: "Glass snakes" actually refer to legless lizards, primarily belonging to the genus Ophisaurus. They are not snakes at all, despite their snake-like appearance. They differ from snakes in several key ways, such as having eyelids and external ear openings.
 
• **Grass snake:** Grass snakes belong to the genus Natrix, specifically in places like Europe. They are non-venomous snakes that live in terrestrial habitats, often near water sources, and are known for their distinctive collar or ring around the neck. They are not fossorial and have functional eyes.

questions.question: Which of the following periods is referred to as a period of stagnant or stationary phase of growth of India’s population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__1901 - 1921__**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Period of stagnant:-**

 
 
• **The period referred to as a "stagnant or stationary phase of growth" of India's population is a demographic concept known as the "demographic transition." **
 
• This refers to the transition from a high birth rate and high death rate society to a low birth rate and low death rate society, typically accompanied by an intermediate phase of rapid population growth.
 
• During the early stages of demographic transition, a country experiences high birth rates due to factors such as lack of family planning, high infant mortality rates (leading to a need for larger families), and traditional cultural norms.
 
• **1901 - 1921 is referred to as a period of stagnant or stationary phase of growth of India’s population.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

questions.question: How many points are there in the 4th set in volleyball?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**25**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Volleyball**:-

 
 
• Volleyball is a team sport.
 
• It is played between two teams of six players.
 
• Teams are separated by a net.
 
• Each team tries to score points by grounding a ball on the other team's court under organised rules.
 
• 
 
Volleyball has come a long way from the dusty-old YMCA gymnasium of Holyoke, Massachusetts, USA.

 
 
• 
 
Dimensions:

 
 
• The dimension of the court is18m/9m.
 
• The width of the net is 1m.
 
• The height of the net is 2.43m for men and 2.24m for women.
 
• A 3 m line in each court is marked to determine the front court and back court.
 
• A regulation volleyball should be 65-67 centimeters in circumference and weigh 260-280 grams.
 
• William G. Morgan invented the sport back in 1895.
 
• It was started because the game of basketball was considered violent.
 
• It was designed as an indoor sport.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Volleyball Pointing System:**

The volleyball point system uses a rally scoring system, meaning a point is awarded on every rally, regardless of which team serves. Here's a breakdown of the key points:

**Sets:**

 
• Most matches are played as best-of-five sets.
 
• The first four sets are played to 25 points, with a two-point lead required to win. So, a set can continue until one team leads by two points, even if the score goes beyond 25-25.
 
• The final set (if necessary) is played to 15 points, again with a two-point lead requirement.

**Scoring:**

A point is awarded to the opposing team whenever your team commits a fault, such as:

 
• Hitting the ball out of bounds.
 
• Touching the net during play.
 
• Four touches by your team before returning the ball over the net.
 
• Foot faults or other technical violations.
 
• Serving errors also result in a point for the opposing team.

questions.question: Who among the following leaders led the Bardoli Satyagraha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vallabhbhai Patel **__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vallabhbhai Patel:-**

 
 
• **He was also related to Bardoli Satyagraha.**
 
• He is known as the Iron Man of India.
 
• The women of Bardoli bestowed the title "Sardar" on Vallabhbhai Patel for his leadership during the Bardoli Satyagraha in 1928.
 
• It was during the struggle and after the Indian National
 
• Congress victory in Bardoli Satyagraha, that Patel first began to be referred to as Sardar.
 
• He is also known as the Bismarck of India because he had played a major role in uniting India.
 
 
 
• **Bardoli Satyagraha:-**
 
 
• **It is an event in the Indian Freedom struggle against the rise in tax during times of financial troubles.**
 
• It took place in the town of Bardoli (Gujarat) in the year 1928.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai (1865 – 1928):-**

 
 
• He is also known as "Punjab Kesari" (Lion of Punjab).
 
• He was an Indian freedom fighter, politician, and social reformer who played a significant role in India's struggle for independence from British rule.
 
• He was born in Punjab, which is now in modern-day Pakistan. Rai was one of the prominent leaders of the Indian National Congress during the early 20th century.
 
 
 
• **Motilal Nehru (1861 – 1931):-**
 
 
• **He** was an Indian lawyer, politician, and prominent leader in the Indian National Congress during the colonial era.
 
• He was a key figure in the Indian independence movement and played a significant role in shaping the political landscape of pre-independence India.
 
• He was the father of Jawaharlal Nehru, who later became the first Prime Minister of India.
 
 
 
• **Chakravarti Rajagopalachari:-**
 
 
• He was commonly known as C. Rajagopalachari or Rajaji (1878 – 1972),
 
• He was an Indian lawyer, statesman, freedom fighter, and one of the prominent leaders in the Indian National Congress.
 
• He played a multifaceted role in the struggle for India's independence and later in the post-independence period.
 
• He is also known for being the last Governor-General of India before the country became a republic.

questions.question: Which of the following is an institutional source of credit in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Commercial bank.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Commercial bank:- **

 
 
• It is an institution that accepts deposit, makes business loans and offer related services to various like accepting deposits and lending loans and advances to general customers and business man.
 
• These institutions run to make profit.
 
• **Commercial banks is an institutional source of credit in India.**
 
• They cater to the financial requirements of industries and various sectors like agriculture, rural development, etc. it is a profit making institution owned by government or private of both.
 
• Commercial bank includes public sector, private sector, foreign banks and regional rural banks:
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Money lenders:-**

 
 
• Money lenders provide an alternative source of credit for individuals and small businesses who may have difficulty accessing loans from formal financial institutions like banks.
 
• This can help to bridge the gap between credit demand and supply.
 
 
 
• **Commission agents:-**
 
 
• Commission agents, also known as brokers or intermediaries, are individuals or firms that facilitate transactions between buyers and sellers in various markets.
 
• They play a significant role in economics by connecting buyers with sellers and helping to efficiently allocate resources.
 
 
 
• **Traders:-**
 
 
• These are individuals or entities that engage in the buying and selling of goods, services, or financial assets with the primary goal of generating profits.
 
• Traders play a significant role in economics and financial markets by facilitating the exchange of assets, contributing to market liquidity, and influencing price movements.

questions.question: In India the State election Commissioner is appointed by the _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **State Election Commissioner (SEC):-**

 
 
• The role of the State Election Commissioner is primarily defined under Article 243K of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It is a crucial constitutional and administrative figure responsible for conducting and supervising elections within a particular state or union territory in India.
 
• **The State Election Commissioner is usually appointed by the Governor of the state. **
 
• The appointment is made after consultation with the State Government, but it is important that the Commissioner is not under the direct influence of the government to ensure the autonomy of the election process.
 
• The tenure of the State Election Commissioner is usually determined by the Governor, and it may vary from state to state. 
 
 
 
• **Governor**:-
 
 
• Governor is the chief executive head of a state.
 
• He is appointed by the President for a term of 5 years and is subjected to pleasure of the President.
 
• The President may transfer a Governor to another state.
 
• The Constitution does not provide any cases of contingency in regard to Governor for example death of the Governor.
 
• Article 160 states that The President can make such provisions as he thinks fit for the discharge of functions of governor in any contingency.

questions.question: Which region has the maximum concentration of iron and steel industries in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chota Nagpur plateau.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chota Nagpur plateau:-**

 
 
• The Chota Nagpur Plateau is known as the 'mineral heart-land of India'.
 
• It is located in eastern India. Most of the parts of Jharkhand state, Orissa, West Bengal, Bihar and Chhattisgarh fall in this plateau.
 
• To its east is the Indus-Ganga Plain and to the south is the Mahanadi.
 
• This plateau is rich in minerals.
 
• Major minerals of India bauxite, mica and coal are found here.
 
• It has the maximum concentration of iron and steel industries in India
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** The Deccan Plateau:**

 
 
• It is a large plateau in western and southern India.
 
• It covers an area of 500,000 square kilometres and extends over eight Indian states.
 
• The word “Deccan” comes from the Sanskrit word Dakshina, meaning “south”.
 
• It lies between the Western and Eastern Ghats and is informally described as the peninsular territory south of the Narmada River between these mountains. 
 
 
 
• **The Malwa Plateau:-**
 
 
• It is a region located in central India, covering parts of the states of Madhya Pradesh and southeastern Rajasthan.
 
• It is characterized by its undulating topography, diverse landscapes, and historical significance.
 
 
 
• **The Chhattisgarh Plateau:-**
 
 
• It is also known as the Chhattisgarh Basin, is a region located in central India, primarily within the state of Chhattisgarh.
 
• It is characterized by its unique geological and geographical features, as well as its cultural and historical significance.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Boron, silicon, antimony.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Metalloids**:-

 
 
• These are elements that have properties similar to both metals and non-metals. In some of their properties, they show similarity with metals and in others with non-metals.
 
• They are hence placed in between metals and non-metals.
 
• Metalloids can also be called semimetals.
 
• They are found in groups 13, 14, 15, 16 and 17 of the p-block.
 
• Metalloids include Boron, Silicon, Germanium, Arsenic, Antimony, Tellurium and Polonium.
 
• Total elements are 118 out of which 91 are metals, 7 are metalloids, and 20 are non-metals.
 
• In the modern periodic table, metalloids are in Right of the periodic table
